text:
This looks like late summer to early autumn 2024. Fed funds is still at 5.33, which means no cut has happened yet. Unemployment is 4.3% and has risen 0.8 points over 12 months. The 2-year and 10-year yields are both about 3.87%, and the 2-year is down 1.02 points over 3 months. Core CPI is 3.21% year over year, and 3.2% fits August 2024 (core was 3.2% in July and 3.3% in August). Headline CPI is 2.92%, close to July 2024's 2.9%.

July 2024 unemployment was 4.3%, and the 3-month average payroll gain was about 170k. That fits. The 10-year yield ended July 2024 at roughly 4.03%, while the 2-year was about 4.26%, which does not match. At the end of August 2024 the 10-year was 3.91% and the 2-year was 3.92%, which is close to the snapshot. August unemployment was 4.2%, though, and the August payroll average was about 116k after revisions. As first published, the August report showed unemployment at 4.2% and payrolls near 150k.

The data may be a mix of vintages, so I'll go with August 2024. The 1-month equity gain of 3.8% matches August, as does developed ex-US up 6.1%. Gold up 2.4% also fits August.
